messages:
Maya (CS): Hey team — TorqLabs onboarding hit continuous 429s during SDK bootstrap after they turned on their proxy pool. Started at ~09:03 PT, persists across regions. I'm looking for quick mitigations + root cause ideas. @Raj any thoughts? :eyes:
Raj (ENG): Thanks, Maya. Do we have the initial client logs? Are these 429s coming from our gateway or from their edge proxy?
Maya (CS): Their snippet pasted in the ticket — they show `HTTP/1.1 429` coming back from our endpoint, but the source IP is their proxy VIP. Logs: `2026-03-18T16:03:12Z embed.create 429 rate_limit exceeded client_id=torqlabs svc=gateway`
Nora (SRE): Can you paste their SDK init code? Sometimes rapid concurrent preflights cause our rate window to trip if all requests look identical.
Maya (CS): Snippet from their Node init: ```js const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference'); const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY, region: 'us-west-2' }); // on server start they do 50 parallel warmups: Promise.all(Array(50).fill(0).map(()=>client.embed('warmup'))); ```
Olivia (Onboard): They mentioned a proxy pool that terminates TLS and reuses a small number of egress IPs. They're trying to warm up 50 containers behind the proxy at once.
Raj (ENG): OK that pattern will *look like* a thundering herd from a few IPs. Two quick mitigations: 1) advise them to stagger warmups (splay) and use jittered backoff; 2) recommend enabling per-worker connection reuse so requests multiplex over HTTP/2 instead of opening new flows — reduces perceived RPS.
Maya (CS): They tried increasing retry attempts but still hit sustained 429s. They asked if we can raise a temporary window for this customer.
Nora (SRE): We can do a one-off bump on their account but prefer to avoid masking the underlying issue. Before that, Raj — can we detect identical client metadata that suggests proxy fanout and apply more lenient rate-smoothing on our side?
Raj (ENG): We have a few levers: token-based rate (per API key), IP-based buckets, and per-route soft limits. If egress IPs are few, IP bucketing is noisy. We can add a temporary rule to weight by API key primarily for that key — that would help. I'll open an internal change request.
Maya (CS): Thanks — customer is asking for an ETA and wants to avoid large changes on their infra. Any interim client-side suggestions I can give them?
Raj (ENG): Tell them: a) instead of Promise.all(50) do a for loop with `await sleep(Math.random()*5000)` between starts; b) set Node HTTP agent maxSockets to 256 and enable keepAlive: `new http.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 256 })`; c) prefer `@redwood/inference` v2.3.1 which defaults to HTTP/2 muxing on supported runtimes. Example: ```js const agent = new http.Agent({ keepAlive:true, maxSockets:256 }); const client = new Redwood({ httpAgent: agent, ... }); ```
Olivia (Onboard): Also advise them to rotate ephemeral tokens more sparingly during warmup — rapid token swaps can inflate preflight auth checks.
Maya (CS): Noted. I'll relay those suggestions. Raj — what's the scope/time for the rule change if we apply API-key weighted smoothing?
Raj (ENG): I'll triage now. If low-risk, Nora can approve for a 2-hour window. Estimate ~20–40 minutes to stage + roll. I'll prepare the rule and the audit notes.
Nora (SRE): I can approve a short window once you post the proposed rule. Post the exact match conditions (api_key only + bypass ip-bucket) and the TTL.
Raj (ENG): Proposed: for api_key=acct_torqlabs_01 set rate smoothing factor=0.5 for 2 hours, log-only first 10 minutes, then enforce. Will attach change in infra runbook.
Maya (CS): Customer asked whether the 429s could be due to scope mismatch on the token — they saw `403` earlier but copied only 429s now. Anything there?
Raj (ENG): 403s would indicate auth/scopes; 429s are rate. If they saw both early, it's possible their token refresh flow returned a limited-scope token for some requests. Ask them to paste the exact 403 payload next time.
Olivia (Onboard): I'll schedule a quick call with TorqLabs for 16:30 PT to walk through the client-side fixes while Raj prepares the rule. Maya, can you confirm meeting and invite?
Maya (CS): Yes — sending invite now. Also pinging customer to throttle warmup until we implement smoothing. :pray:
Raj (ENG): Change prepared, posting runbook snippet here: ```yaml # infra-rule change match: api_key: acct_torqlabs_01 override: rate_bucket: api_key primary smoothing: 0.5 ttl: 2h audit_mode: true -> 10m then enforce``` Nora please flip when ready.
Nora (SRE): Approved — will apply after the 10m audit window. Watch for any unexpected error patterns, but should be safe.
Maya (CS): TorqLabs confirms they paused the parallel warmups and will join the 16:30 call. They asked if we can share a short checklist to avoid future onboarding bursts. I'll draft and send to them after the call.
Olivia (Onboard): Great. Follow-ups: - Raj: post final rule diff and rollback steps to the ticket - Nora: apply & monitor - Maya: run the checklist call and capture customer's feedback - Me (Olivia): add a note to onboarding playbook about recommending staggered warmups and agent keepAlive
Maya (CS): Thanks everyone. I'll update the ticket with the runbook link and close the loop after the call. :white_check_mark:
